regulation_access.value: PRIIPs Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 applies from 1 January 2018; a manufacturer must draw up a KID and a person advising on or selling a PRIIP to a retail investor must provide it before the investor is bound. US ETF issuers do not publish PRIIPs KIDs, so most EU brokers block retail BUY orders of US-domiciled ETFs; existing positions can usually be held/sold.
regulation_access.note: justETF article 28 Mar 2018 ('you won't be able to buy more'); EUR-Lex text could not be fetched (bot challenge). Article numbers (Art. 5, 13) confirmed via ČNB Q&A RS2018-12.

regulation_access.value: UCITS funds were exempt from PRIIPs KID until 31 Dec 2022 (Reg. (EU) 2021/2259); since 1 Jan 2023 UCITS ETFs sold to retail must have a PRIIPs KID too - which is why UCITS twins are available.

ČNB (Czech National Bank) Q&A RS2018-12 (22 Oct 2018): a securities dealer that only provides execution-only service on the client's own instruction / access to a foreign exchange, without offering or advising on the product, does not 'sell' a PRIIP in the sense of Art. 4(5) and is not subject to the Art. 13(1) KID-delivery duty (but must still act with due care and give risk information, § 15d ZPKT). This is the legal basis that lets some Czech-licensed brokers (Fio) offer US ETFs to retail clients.
regulation_access.note: Verbatim: 'Pokud tedy obchodník s cennými papíry provádí pouze execution-only služby v návaznosti na podnět investora ... nelze jej považovat za subjekt povinnosti podle čl. 13 odst. 1 nařízení PRIIPs.'

regulation_access.value: Professional client on request (MiFID II Annex II, transposed in CZ as § 2b(1)(b) zákon 256/2004 Sb.): must meet at least 2 of 3 - (1) in each of the last 4 consecutive quarters, trades of significant size averaging at least 10 per quarter; (2) assets in cash + investment instruments of at least EUR 500,000; (3) at least 1 year working in the financial market in a role requiring knowledge of the transactions. Professional clients lose part of retail protection; PRIIPs KID duty does not apply to them.
regulation_access.note: Czech law text read on zakonyprolidi.cz; EUR-Lex original not fetched

regulation_access.value: IBKR's knowledge base (PRIIPs Overview): US ETF issuers generally don't produce KIDs, so EEA/UK retail clients cannot buy them; listed alternatives: European-issued equivalents, CFDs on large US ETFs issued by IBKR's EU entities, or reclassification as professional client. Individual clients are 'Retail' by default.

tax_notes.value: US withholding on dividends paid to foreign persons is 30% by default; reduced treaty rates apply when the beneficial owner certifies foreign status (Form W-8BEN).

Czech-US tax treaty (Sdělení č. 32/1994 Sb.), Art. 10(2)(b): portfolio dividends max 15% US tax; Art. 10(3): 15% rate explicitly applies to dividends from a US Regulated Investment Company (US ETFs are RICs).

Czech tax on foreign dividends: can go into the separate tax base under § 8(8) ZDP taxed at 15% (§ 16a(1)); US tax withheld up to the treaty rate (15%) is credited, so with W-8BEN the total is ~15%; without W-8BEN 30% is withheld and only 15% is creditable (the rest must be reclaimed from the IRS).
tax_notes.note: Rates verified in the law text; the 'credit max 15%' mechanics confirmed by e15.cz (2026-04-27) on a German example: 'v daňovém přiznání se započte maximálně 15 procent'.

tax_notes.value: Irish-domiciled UCITS ETFs: under the US-Ireland treaty, portfolio dividends from US companies to the Irish fund are generally taxed at 15% (instead of 30%). This 15% is lost inside the fund; the Czech investor cannot credit it.
tax_notes.note: Treaty technical explanation: 'Other dividends are generally taxable at 15 percent.' 'Cannot credit' is our inference (the investor receives no US-source dividend), not a quoted source.

tax_notes.value: Accumulating ETF: no distribution -> no dividend income to report; gain taxed only on sale (and exempt after the 3-year time test). Distributing ETF: distributions taxed at 15% in CZ.
Time test (časový test): income from sale of a security is exempt if more than 3 years passed between acquisition and sale - § 4(1)(u) ZDP.
Value test: income from sales of securities is exempt if the TOTAL (gross proceeds, not profit) in the tax year does not exceed CZK 100,000 - § 4(1)(t) ZDP.

CZK 40 million cap: introduced from 1 Jan 2025 (consolidation package) for time-test-exempt income from securities and business shares; ABOLISHED for securities and business shares from 1 Jan 2026 by zákon č. 360/2025 Sb.; it remains only for crypto-assets (§ 4(3) ZDP now refers only to § 4(1)(zk) crypto). Sales made in 2025 are still under the cap.
tax_notes.note: Current § 4(3) text read directly; law number 360/2025 Sb. from Forvis Mazars / dauc.cz via search summary; MF press release https://mf.gov.cz/cs/ministerstvo/media/tiskove-zpravy/2025/zmeny-v-daneni-prodeje-podilu-ve-firmach-a-akcii-a-61234

tax_notes.value: Reporting duty: an exempt income above CZK 5,000,000 must be reported to the tax office by the tax-return deadline (§ 38v ZDP).
Personal income tax rate 2025: 15% up to tax base CZK 1,676,052, 23% above.
Unified FX rates for tax year 2025 (Pokyn GFŘ-D-75): 1 EUR = 24.66 CZK, 1 USD = 21.84 CZK.

US estate tax for non-resident non-citizens: return (Form 706-NA) required if US-situated assets exceed USD 60,000; US-situs includes stock of US corporations (US-domiciled ETFs = US corporations/trusts - our reading). Max unified credit USD 13,000 (= tax on the first USD 60,000). Rate schedule goes from 18% up to 40% above USD 1,000,000.
